title: API config design scratchpad - routing & batching
content:
Notes to self - rough brain dump (informal)

Context:
- Working on a lightweight, extensible API-side config spec for runtime routing + batching + caching + model variant fallbacks. Goal is something teams can check into app repos and also reference from Console.
- Need to support: per-route policies, tenant overrides, canary rollouts, autoscaling hints, and cost-aware fallbacks.
- Keep the surface small for MVP; iterate on richer policies later.

Goals/principles:
- Declarative but composable: routes reference reusable policy blocks (eg batching-profile, routing-policy).
- Human-editable YAML/JSON. Console shows visualized effective config (merge/overrides).
- Safe defaults: no disruptive rollouts by default, explicit canary flags.
- Backwards compatible: unknown fields ignored (forward-compat).

High-level components:
- route: the API path / logical feature (eg /chat, /embeddings)
- modelPool: list of model variants (with cost/latency metadata)
- routingPolicy: selectors + priorities (latency-first, cost-first, region)
- fallbackPolicy: rules when primary model unavailable (map to modelPool entry)
- batchingProfile: target max_batch_latency_ms, max_batch_tokens, packing strategy
- kvCachePolicy: enabled, ttl, prefixKey (for prefix caching)
- rollout: canary percentage, stages, rollback triggers

Sketch: API config shape (YAML-ish) - rough

route: chat_v1
  description: quick chat route for webclient
  modelPool:
    - id: gpt-like-16k-quant
      priority: 10
      cost_score: 1.0
      latency_p50_ms: "40-60"
      tags: ["quantized", "low-cost"]
    - id: gpt-like-16k-fp16
      priority: 5
      cost_score: 3.2
      latency_p50_ms: "30-40"
      tags: ["fp16", "higher-quality"]
  routingPolicy:
    strategy: "latency-weighted" # other: cost-first, balanced, region-aware
    constraints:
      region: ["us-west-2", "us-east-1"]
      max_latency_ms: 120
  fallbackPolicy:
    fallback_order: ["gpt-like-16k-fp16", "gpt-like-8k-quant"]
    on_error: "retry-with-fallback" # or "fail-fast"
  batchingProfile:
    max_wait_ms: 8
    max_batch_tokens: 2048
    packing: "prefix-aware" # try to pack short prompts together
  kvCachePolicy:
    enabled: true
    ttl_seconds: 3600
    cache_prefix: "chat_v1:prefixhash"
  rollout:
    mode: "canary"
    canary_percent: 10
    metrics: ["latency_p95", "token_error_rate"]
    rollback_thresholds:
      latency_p95_increase_pct: 15
      error_rate_absolute: 0.02

Notes on batchingProfile:
- max_wait_ms tradeoff: lower => lower p95 latency for small requests but worse cost. 8ms is a starting idea for webchat.
- packing: try to implement prefix-aware packing so we don't group hugely different seq lengths (wasteful). That can be a runtime hint, not a hard rule.

Routing policy ideas:
- simple priority-list (pick highest priority model with capacity) is easiest to implement.
- latency-weighted: use model profiles + current load estimate to score choices.
- region-aware: prefer model variants in same region, fallback to cross-region only when necessary.
- cost-floor: allow routingPolicy to specify max_cost_score (prevent expensive models for low-tier tenants).

Model metadata (what the runtime needs):
- id, architecture, quantization, p50/p95 latency typical, cost_score (relative), supported_sequence_length, tokenization (bpe/vocab id), compatibility_tags

Example: request-level override (runtime headers)
- x-redwood-model-hint: "prefer=fp16;fall_back=quant;max_cost=2.0"
- Should be limited by tenant policy and console UI (only allowed for dev/test keys)

Open questions / TODOs:
- How to represent capacity constraints? (static capacity vs dynamic estimate). For MVP use a soft capacity boolean + runtime live metric for actual throttling.
- Where to store configs? Git-first (app repo) + Console copy synced to central store. Need a reconciliation/merge UI.
- Rollouts: tie to metrics from Console (evals) and allow automatic rollback. Need a simple API for register metric hooks.
- Namespaces/tenants: default inheritance (org -> project -> route). Merge precedence: project overrides org overrides default.
- Validation: add lightweight schema (JSON Schema) and runtime defensive checks.

Tradeoffs to keep in doc:
- Simplicity vs expressiveness: prefer slightly simpler spec now; add advanced selectors later.
- Declarative vs imperative: declarative config easier to reason but we still need small imperative hooks (eg on_error: retry-with-backoff). Keep imperative minimal.

Small wire API sketch for route config lookup:
- GET /v1/configs/effective?route=chat_v1&project=my-app -> returns merged effective config (JSON)
- POST /v1/configs/validate (body: yaml/json) -> returns schema validation + warnings

Quick implementation roadmap (MVP):
1) Define JSON Schema (core fields: route, modelPool, routingPolicy, batchingProfile, rollout)
2) Implement merge precedence (org -> project -> route) and minimal validation on write
3) Add Console UI to display merged config and quick edit for canary percentage
4) Add runtime adapter to translate config -> runtime hints (score function for routing, batching params)
5) Collect telemetry: route-level p50/p95, cost-per-token, fallback counts, canary metric deltas

Notes for follow-ups (links/owners):
- Casey: prototype runtime adapter (routing score) - assign
- Jamie: Console merge UI + visualize modelPool tradeoffs - assign
- Samir: JSON Schema + validation endpoint - assign

Rough todos (personal):
- [ ] Draft initial JSON Schema (fields + minimal docs)
- [ ] Add examples for embeddings route and batch inference route
- [ ] Write RFC-style doc once sketch stabilizes
- [ ] Sync with SRE on capacity signals and metrics available

Random thoughts / scribbles:
- Could expose a small DSL for fallback conditions (eg if p95 > X for Y seconds) but probably overkill for MVP.
- Should include metadata for billing tags so console can show cost delta per route/model variant.
- Consider soft-constraints vs hard-constraints in routing policy; start with soft and a debug mode for strict enforcement.

End of scratchpad.

-- ryan
